reading.text:
Unit: spec Dissertation.PaperSpec.A.eq_uniq_fwd (claim A:rem:uniq-no-integ, Remark 3.4; the clause
is the forward step of the membership proof of Theorem 3.3, sections/03-main-results.tex
lines 144-156).

Printed step: "Since the two solutions have the same initial condition, the forward equation is
delta X_t = int_0^t delta b_s ds + int_0^t delta sigma_s dW_s + int_0^t int_E delta h_s(e)
Ntilde(ds, de). By Cauchy-Schwarz, the BDG inequality and the compensation formula,
E sup_{0<=t<=T} |delta X_t|^2 <= C_T E int_0^T (|delta b_s|^2 + |delta sigma_s|_F^2
+ ||delta h_s||^2) ds < infinity by (3.2), so delta X in S^2(0,T;R^n)."
Remark 3.4 claims the membership steps from the Lipschitz control alone.

A faithful formal statement must contain:
- setting of Section 2 (common part below); hypotheses (2.3), Assumption 2.3, two tuples in
  H^2_weak solving (1.1) for one coefficient system with the SAME initial datum (this is used:
  xi_0 cancels);
- conclusion (a), the forward difference identity: for every t in [0,T], a.s. (every t, not
  a.e. t): X^1_t - X^2_t = int_0^t delta b_s ds + int_0^t delta sigma_s dW_s
  + int_0^t int_E delta h_s(e) Ntilde(ds, de), delta h at the predictable tuples; the
  stochastic integrals are the Ito and compensated Poisson integrals (difference integrands in
  L^2 by (3.2)); the ds-integral the honest difference of the drift integrals (no junk values);
- conclusion (b), the maximal bound: a constant C_T whose dependence is that of the printed
  subscript and proof: Cauchy-Schwarz (factor T), BDG (universal c_BDG) and the compensation
  formula, i.e. C_T depends only on T (and the universal BDG constant), NOT on L, the
  coefficients, nu, the dimensions or the two solutions. Quantifier order: C_T chosen (as a
  function of T, or existentially) BEFORE the coefficients and the solutions. A statement with
  C chosen after the solutions would be weaker than printed (it would only say the left side is
  finite when the right side is positive). The bound:
  E sup_{0<=t<=T} |delta X_t|^2 <= C_T * E int_0^T (|delta b_s|^2 + |delta sigma_s|_F^2
  + ||delta h_s||^2_{L^2(nu)}) ds, with the expectations in [0, infinity] (supremum over all
  t in [0,T], not an essential supremum or a supremum over a countable set unless equivalent by
  cadlag paths);
- conclusion (c): the right side is finite ("< infinity by (3.2)"), hence delta X in S^2.
- Broader than the step in the proof (2.4-2.5 dropped), which is what Remark 3.4 asserts.
- non-degenerate witness: two different solutions with delta X (and delta b or delta sigma or
  delta h) nonzero.

Common setting and hypotheses (sections/02-model-assumptions.tex, sections/03-main-results.tex,
proof of Theorem 3.3 and Remark 3.4).

Setting (standing setting of Section 2). A filtered probability space with the usual conditions,
horizon T > 0, dimensions n, m, d >= 1, a d-dimensional Brownian motion W and an independent
Poisson random measure N on R_+ x E with intensity dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably
generated (E, calE) (nu(E) = infinity admitted: no finiteness of nu may be assumed); the
filtration is the usual augmentation of the one generated by W, N and an independent F_0.
State space H = R^n x R^m x R^{m x d} x L^2(nu; R^m) with |theta|_H^2 = |x|^2 + |y|^2 + |z|_F^2
+ ||u||^2. Coefficients b, sigma, h, f (on [0,T] x H x P_2(H)) and g (on R^n x P_2(R^n)) are
deterministic and jointly Borel; for h, Borel measurability of (t, theta, mu) -> h(t, theta, ., mu)
into L^2(nu; R^n), which is (2.3).

Hypotheses in force for the clauses of this chunk (as the clause names say): (2.3) and
Assumption 2.3 only. Assumption 2.3: some L >= 0 such that for a.e. t and all diagonal inputs
(Theta, Law Theta), (Theta', Law Theta') at time t (Theta in L^2(Omega, F_t; H)),
|db| + |dsigma|_F + ||dh|| + |df| <= L(|dX| + |dY| + |dZ|_F + ||dU|| + W_2(mu, mu')) a.s., and
for all X_T, X'_T in L^2(Omega, F_T; R^n), |dg_T| <= L(|X_T - X'_T| + W_2(rho, rho')) a.s.
NOT assumed: Assumption 2.2 (origin integrability), 2.4 (G), 2.5 (monotonicity). In the printed
proof of Theorem 3.3 Assumptions 2.3-2.5 are in force; Remark 3.4 says that the membership
Theta^1 - Theta^2 in S is shown "using only the Lipschitz control of coefficient differences",
i.e. the membership steps are claimed from Assumption 2.3 (no 2.2). A clause stated under (2.3)
and 2.3 alone is therefore broader than the step inside the proof of Theorem 3.3 (instantiation:
add 2.4-2.5 and discard them) and is what Remark 3.4 claims for the membership steps.

Two tuples Theta^k = (X^k, Y^k, Z^k, U^k), k = 1, 2, in H^2_weak (paper's \Hweak = H^2):
X^k, Y^k cadlag adapted with E int_0^T |.|^2 dt < infinity; Z^k predictable with
E int |Z|_F^2 < infinity; U^k predictable (P x calE-measurable representative) with
E int ||U||^2 < infinity. Each satisfies (1.1) with the SAME initial datum xi_0: forward identity
X_t = xi_0 + int_0^t b(s, Theta_s, mu_s) ds + int_0^t sigma(...) dW + int_0^t int_E
h(s, Theta_s^-, e, mu_s^-) Ntilde(ds, de) a.s. for every t, and backward identity
Y_t = g(X_T, Law X_T) + int_t^T f(s, Theta_s, mu_s) ds - int_t^T Z dW - int_t^T int_E U Ntilde
a.s. for every t; the integrals in (1.1) must exist for the identities to make sense (the
terminal condition presupposes Law(X_T) in P_2, i.e. X_T in L^2). mu_t = Law(Theta_t),
mu_t^- = Law(Theta_t^-) with Theta_t^- = (X_{t-}, Y_{t-}, Z_t, U_t) (Borel representatives of
Lemma A.1, equal to the laws for a.e. t). Both solutions use the SAME coefficient system
(single system), and the differences of the uniqueness proof are
delta psi_t = psi(t, Theta^1_t, mu^1_t) - psi(t, Theta^2_t, mu^2_t), psi in {b, sigma, f},
delta h_t = h(t, Theta^{1,-}_t, ., mu^{1,-}_t) - h(t, Theta^{2,-}_t, ., mu^{2,-}_t) in L^2(nu),
delta g_T = g(X^1_T, Law X^1_T) - g(X^2_T, Law X^2_T), delta Theta = Theta^1 - Theta^2
(not the two-system differences of Theorem 3.1).

Witness expectation: the hypotheses can be met by an instance the paper intends only with two
DIFFERENT solutions (under Assumptions 2.3-2.5 the solutions coincide, every delta vanishes and
each bound reads 0 <= 0). Since the clauses are stated under 2.3 alone, a Lipschitz system with
two distinct solutions with the same initial datum (e.g. a deterministic linear system such as
X' = Y, Y' = -X, g = 0 on T = pi/2, which has the family X = A sin t, Y = A cos t) is an
instance Remark 3.4's claim covers; the witness should make the relevant delta quantities
nonzero. A witness with Theta^1 = Theta^2 is degenerate.

Definitional points to check: expectations and time integrals of nonnegative quantities should
be in [0, infinity] (or integrability must be asserted), not Bochner integrals whose junk value
0 for non-integrable functions would make an inequality or a finiteness claim trivial; the
stochastic integrals must be the Ito and compensated Poisson integrals of the paper, and the
solution predicate must not be satisfiable through junk values of undefined integrals (under
2.3 alone the individual coefficient processes need not be square integrable).

comparison.text:
Comparison for Dissertation.PaperSpec.A.eq_uniq_fwd (claim A:rem:uniq-no-integ, Remark 3.4; the
forward step of the proof of Theorem 3.3, lines 144-156, under the Lipschitz control alone).

- Setting, hypotheses: as read (shared part); same initial datum xi0 for both tuples (used: xi0
  cancels). No 2.2, 2.4, 2.5: what Remark 3.4 claims; broader than the printed step (instance: add
  2.4-2.5).
- Constant: `exists K : R -> R` before the setting, T, L, the coefficients and the solutions; the
  bound uses K(T). The printed C_T comes from Cauchy-Schwarz (T), BDG (universal c_BDG) and the
  compensation formula: a function of T alone. Matches the reading (chosen first; not after the
  solutions, which would have weakened the bound).
- Conclusion (a), forward identity, for each coordinate i: a.s. integrable paths of delta b_i on
  [0,T] (honest ds-integral); delta sigma_i meets the conditions of the d-dimensional Ito
  integral; there is a measurable, marked progressive, finite-energy H equal to delta h_i
  (coeffJump at the predictable tuples) a.e. for P x dt|[0,T] x nu, and for EVERY such H, for every
  t in [0,T], a.s.
  X^1_i(t) - X^2_i(t) = int_{[0,t]} delta b_i ds + I_W(delta sigma_i)(t) + I_N(H)(t).
  This is the printed identity, "for every t, a.s.", the Poisson integral read through a
  representative of delta h as (2.4) prescribes; quantifying over every representative makes it
  independent of the choice. Matches.
- Conclusion (b): int^- sup_{t in [0,T]} |delta X_t|^2 dP
  <= K(T) (sum_i energy(delta b_i) + sum_{i,j} energy(delta sigma_ij) + sum_i markedEnergy(delta h_i)),
  i.e. E sup_{t<=T}|delta X_t|^2 <= C_T E int_0^T (|delta b|^2 + |delta sigma|_F^2 + ||delta h||^2) ds,
  sup over all of [0,T], all in [0, infinity]. Matches.
- Conclusion (c): the same right-hand sum < infinity ("< infinity by (3.2)"). Matches; delta X in
  S^2 follows.
- Nothing narrower: every t, every coordinate, all three channels; no extra hypothesis.

Coverage (A:rem:uniq-no-integ in acceptance/claims.json). The remark asserts: (a) Remark 3.2 would
place each H^2_weak tuple satisfying (1.1) in S under Assumption 2.2 -- clause rem_cwp_class;
(b) uniqueness requires only Assumptions 2.3-2.5 -- clause thm_uniq; (c) for that, only the
membership Theta^1 - Theta^2 in S is needed, shown using only the Lipschitz control of coefficient
differences -- the four clauses eq_uniq_coeff_lip ((3.2)), eq_uniq_fwd (forward identity and
estimate), eq_uniq_bwd_lip ((3.3)) and rem_uniq_lip_mem (the membership), all under (2.3) and
Assumption 2.3 alone, with the bound before (3.2) and the backward identity stated in
A:eq:uniq-coeff and A:eq:uniq-bwd; (d) "the proof of Theorem 3.5 uses Assumption 2.2" -- a
description of a proof, recorded in the scope note as no separate claim, which I accept; (e)
xi0 in L^2 is necessary for a solution in S -- rem_uniq_initial; (f) the origin-value conditions
are sufficient but not necessary -- rem_uniq_singular (sufficiency being Theorem 3.5); (g) the
t^{-1/2} drift and the shift X -> X - 2 sqrt t -- rem_uniq_translation. So the clauses together
state every mathematical assertion of the passage at this revision. The four Lipschitz-only
clauses state what (c) claims: "using only the Lipschitz control" means the membership steps need
Assumption 2.3 (with the standing (2.3)) and nothing else -- not 2.2 (the point of the remark) and
not 2.4-2.5 (unused by those steps) -- so their hypotheses are those (c) puts in force; relative to
the printed steps inside the proof of Theorem 3.3, where 2.3-2.5 hold, they are broader, the
printed steps being the instances with 2.4-2.5 added. No clause states something the passage does
not claim. Witness: rem_uniq_lip_hypotheses has two different solutions of a Lipschitz system
that fails 2.5, so the Lipschitz-only clauses are not read at coinciding solutions (where every
delta vanishes); its nonzero quantities are delta X, delta Y, delta b, delta f, delta g_T, while
delta sigma, delta h, delta Z, delta U vanish and nu is a one-atom finite measure; it also
satisfies Assumption 2.2, so it does not exhibit the "without origin integrability" generality
(that is exhibited separately by rem_uniq_singular / rem_uniq_translation).
For this clause in particular: at the witness delta b = cos t and delta X = sin t are nonzero,
but delta sigma = delta h = 0, so the Brownian and Poisson integrals of the forward identity and
their terms in the bound vanish there.

Shared observations (Lean read in Dissertation/PaperSpec/A/Sec3UniquenessLip.lean,
Dissertation/PaperSpec/A/Setting.lean, Dissertation/WellPosedness/System/PaperWeakSolutionInt.lean,
Dissertation/WellPosedness/System/PaperWeakSolution.lean, Dissertation/WellPosedness/Spec/Assumptions.lean,
Dissertation/WellPosedness/System/Solves.lean, Dissertation/WellPosedness/Existence/CoeffBorel.lean,
Dissertation/Law/LawP2.lean, Dissertation/WellPosedness/System/Tuple.lean,
Dissertation/WellPosedness/Enlarged/Filtration.lean, the LevyStochCalc energies and integrals, and
the witness Dissertation/Acceptance/A/WitnessRotation.lean).

Setting. Universe-polymorphic probability space, a LevyDriver (d-dimensional Brownian motion and a
Poisson random measure with sigma-finite intensity nu on a countably generated E, sigma(W) and
sigma(N) independent; no finiteness of nu), an initial sigma-algebra G0 independent of the driver,
filtration enlJoint = usual augmentation (right-continuous, null sets) of the driver filtration
joined with G0; n, m, d > 0; T > 0. Matches Section 2.

Hypotheses. JointBorel T C is (2.3): b, sigma, h (into L^2(nu; R^n)), f Borel on
[0,T] x H x (P_2(H), W_2), g Borel on R^n x (P_2(R^n), W_2). Assumption23 over enlJoint is
Assumption 2.3 as printed: L >= 0; for a.e. t in [0,T], for all diagonal inputs (strongly
F_t-measurable square-integrable Theta, with lawP2), a.s. the sum of the four coefficient
differences <= L (sum of the four channel norms + W_2 of the Hilbert norm); and the terminal
bound (2.6). No Assumption 2.2, 2.4, 2.5. One coefficient system C and one initial datum xi0 for
both tuples, as in the proof of Theorem 3.3. Matches "under (2.3) and Assumption 2.3 alone".

Solution notion WeakSolution (H^2_weak): X, Y adapted on [0,T], every path right-continuous on
[0,T) with left limits on (0,T] (cadlag), finite energy E int_0^T |.|^2; Z predictable, U marked
predictable, both vanishing off [0,T] with finite energy; drift and driver processes along Theta
jointly and progressively measurable with almost every path integrable on [0,T] (only pathwise:
no square integrability of b, f along Theta is required, which keeps the generality of Remark 3.4,
no Assumption 2.2); the diffusion process and a jump integrand gamma (a representative of
h(s, Theta^-_s, ., mu^-_s) in L^2(nu), a.e. s, a.s.) with finite energy, so the L^2 stochastic
integrals exist; X_T square integrable (the paper: Law(X_T) in P_2 is presupposed); both
identities of (1.1) a.s. simultaneously for all t in [0,T] (Brownian integral through a cadlag
version). Representation choice to note: the diffusion and jump coefficients along a solution are
required to have finite energy. This is harmless: the coefficients are deterministic, and with
Assumption 2.3 applied at (Theta_t, mu_t) and the diagonal input (0, delta_0), the existence of
the (even local) L^2 stochastic integrals of sigma and h along a tuple of H^2_weak forces
sigma(., 0, delta_0) and h(., 0, delta_0) into L^2(0,T), hence finite energy along the tuple;
the drift is the only channel in which Remark 3.4's example (t^{-1/2}) lives, and the Lean keeps
it pathwise.

Coefficient processes. driftProc, diffusionProc, driverProc evaluate C at (s, Theta_s(omega),
lawP2 P Theta_s) (Theta_s = tupleAt, U lifted to its L^2(nu) class); lawP2 is the image law when
Theta_s is square integrable and the Dirac mass at 0 otherwise, which happens only at a Lebesgue
null set of times for a tuple of H^2_weak, so it agrees with the paper's Borel law flow for a.e.
t, which is all the processes are used for. delta h is taken through coeffJump applied to
(leftLimProc X, leftLimProc Y, Z, U): the canonical jointly measurable representative of
h(s, Theta^-_s, ., mu^-_s) with mu^-_s = lawP2 of the predictable tuple; this is the paper's
delta h_t at the predictable tuples. terminalVal is g(X_T, lawP2 X_T), the true law since X_T is
in L^2. All squared norms are esq sums of squared coordinates (Euclidean and Frobenius norms) and
the L^2(nu) norms are sum_k int^- |.|^2 dnu; expectations, time integrals and suprema are
[0, infinity]-valued (lintegral, energy, markedEnergy, iSup over t in [0,T]): no Bochner junk
value can make an inequality or a finiteness claim trivial.

Witness rem_uniq_lip_hypotheses: d = 1, nu = Dirac at 0 on R, G0 trivial, n = m = 1, T = pi/4,
coefficients b = y, sigma = z, h = u, f = x, g = x (affine, L = 1); JointBorel and Assumption23
are proved, and (sin t, cos t, 0, 0) and the zero tuple are WeakSolutions from xi0 = 0, with
delta X_t = sin t and delta Y_t = cos t; the theorem also shows Assumption 2.5 fails for every
full-rank G. So the hypotheses are met with two DIFFERENT solutions, at a system satisfying 2.3
and not 2.5. Non-zero along the witness: delta X, delta Y, delta b = cos t, delta f = sin t,
delta g_T = sin(pi/4). Zero along the witness: delta sigma, delta h, delta Z, delta U (Z = U = 0
for both tuples), and nu is a finite one-atom measure; the witness also satisfies Assumption 2.2
(origin values 0). So the instance is non-degenerate in the drift, driver, terminal and state
channels, but the Brownian and Poisson channels of each clause vanish there (their stochastic
integrals read 0 = 0) and the infinite-activity and no-origin-integrability regimes are not
exhibited by this witness.

verdict.detail:
Representation choices, each harmless:
1. Solution class (WeakSolution): drift and driver along a solution only pathwise integrable (this
   keeps Remark 3.4's point, no Assumption 2.2), while the diffusion and the jump coefficient along
   a solution have finite energy (L^2 stochastic integrals). With deterministic coefficients and
   Assumption 2.3 at the diagonal input (0, delta_0), any tuple of H^2_weak along which the (even
   local) L^2 integrals of sigma and h exist has sigma(., 0, delta_0), h(., 0, delta_0) in
   L^2(0,T), so finite energy along it; no solution the paper intends is excluded. X_T in L^2 is
   what Law(X_T) in P_2 presupposes. Every path cadlag, identities a.s. for all t at once.
2. Laws through lawP2 (image law in L^2, Dirac at 0 otherwise): differs from the Borel law flow of
   Lemma A.1 only at a Lebesgue-null set of times, where the processes are not used.
3. delta h through the canonical jointly measurable representative coeffJump at the predictable
   tuple (X_-, Y_-, Z, U) and its law; Poisson integrands read through an a.e.-equal measurable,
   marked progressive representative of finite energy, as (2.4) prescribes.
4. Vectors as coordinates: squared Euclidean / Frobenius norms as sums of squared coordinates,
   the L^2(nu; R^j) norm as sum_k int^- |.|^2 dnu; expectations, time integrals and suprema in
   [0, infinity] (lintegral, energy, markedEnergy, iSup over t in [0,T]); these are exact and
   leave no junk value.
5. Filtration enlJoint: the usual augmentation of the driver filtration joined with an
   independent G0 -- the filtration of Section 2.
6. The constant C_T as a function K of T chosen before everything, the printed dependence (T and the
   universal BDG constant).

author_review.disagreements:
1. Verdict class. The author records "faithful"; I record "faithful with representation choices",
   listing the choices: (a) the solution notion requires the diffusion and jump coefficients along
   each solution to have finite energy (L^2 stochastic integrals), while the drift and driver are
   only pathwise integrable. This is harmless: with deterministic coefficients and Assumption 2.3
   at (0, delta_0), the existence of the stochastic integrals along an H^2_weak tuple forces it.
   (b) Laws through lawP2, which has a junk Dirac value only at Lebesgue-null times. (c) delta h
   through coeffJump at the predictable tuple. (d) Coordinates and [0, infinity]-valued
   expectations and suprema. (e) The enlarged, augmented filtration. On the meaning there is no
   disagreement: hypotheses (2.3) and Assumption 2.3 alone are what Remark 3.4's "using only the
   Lipschitz control" puts in force, and the printed steps of the proof of Theorem 3.3 are the
   instances with 2.4-2.5 added.
2. Witness. The author writes that every bound has a nonzero left side at the witness, which is
   true. Also true, and not recorded: delta sigma, delta h, delta Z and delta U vanish there
   (Z = U = 0, sigma = z, h = u), and nu is a one-atom finite measure. So the Brownian and Poisson
   channels of the forward identity, of the estimates and of the membership are 0 at the witness.
   The witness also satisfies Assumption 2.2, so it does not exhibit the "without origin
   integrability" case that gives Remark 3.4 its title. That case is exhibited separately by the
   t^{-1/2} clauses. The instance is non-degenerate (two different solutions) but exercises only
   the drift, driver, terminal and state channels.
